decision_rule: Admit a new objective candidate only if the combined M128 fixed-batch loss improves repeatably while M124 behavior retention and zero-response gap are preserved; do not admit PPO from objective loss alone.
failure_criteria: combined M128 loss improvement is not repeatable
normal behavior retention regresses below M124
zero-response or wrong-history behavior gap disappears
the result is treated as driver success without behavior and intervention gates
hypothesis: The deduplicated M128 accepted-only corpus gives a stronger outcome-centric self-ID objective than the smaller M122 corpus. A retention-anchored M124 continuation should reduce the combined loss without degrading behavior.
success_criteria: M128 fixed-batch loss improves on repeated seeds
history ablations retain an outcome gap
source-side limitation remains documented before PPO
